cards.text: One day an expert in the law, a man who studies God's Law, stands up to test Jesus. 'Teacher,' he asks, 'what must I do to inherit eternal life?' Quizzing the Teacher takes nerve, friend, like a new hire on day one handing the boss a pop quiz.

cards.question: When the expert in the law asks what he must do to inherit eternal life, Jesus answers him with a question of His own.

cards.text: Jesus asks back, 'What is written in the Law?' and 'How do you read it?' Asking a law expert about the Law is like asking ME about cookies, so pull up a chair, because this man is READY.

cards.question: Jesus asks the expert what the Law says. The expert answers with two commands. What are they about?

answers.text: Loving God and loving your neighbor
Keeping the Sabbath and giving offerings
Honoring parents and telling the truth

cards.text: He answers, 'Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind' and 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Heart, soul, strength AND mind, friend, that's the whole batch down to the last crumb.

cards.question: Jesus tells the expert in the law that he answered correctly.
The expert asked how to inherit eternal life. Jesus tells him that to live, he has to ___ what those two commands say.

cards.text: Jesus just told him he's right. Case closed? NOPE, because the expert has one more question for Jesus.

cards.question: Jesus told the expert he answered correctly. What does the expert ask Jesus next?

answers.text: And how often should I pray

cards.question: The expert in the law asks Jesus who his neighbor is because he wants to ___ himself.

cards.text: Jesus takes up the expert's question and answers with a story. A man is going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he falls into the hands of robbers.

cards.question: In Jesus' story, the robbers strip the man on the road to Jericho and ___ him before they go away.

cards.text: They strip him, beat him and leave him half dead. Then, by chance, a priest comes down the same road and sees him.

cards.question: A priest sees the man the robbers left half dead. What does the priest do?

answers.text: He passes by on the other side
He runs to the next town for help
He stops and prays over the man

cards.text: Next a Levite, a man from the tribe of Levi, comes to that same spot. He sees the man too.

cards.question: The Levite sees the hurt man on the road and stops to help him.

cards.text: Then a Samaritan, a man from the land of Samaria, comes upon him on a journey. John's Gospel tells us Jews didn't associate with Samaritans (John 4:9).

cards.question: When the Samaritan sees the man the robbers left half dead, he has ___.

cards.text: The Samaritan goes to him. He bandages his wounds, pouring on oil and wine.

cards.question: The Samaritan has bandaged the hurt man's wounds. How does he get the man off the road?

answers.text: He puts him on his own animal
He carries him on his back
He waves down a passing cart

cards.question: The Samaritan puts the hurt man on his own animal. Where does he bring him?
At the inn, the Samaritan takes care of the hurt man himself.

cards.text: His OWN animal, friend, and I won't even lend out my apron. The next day he takes out two denarii and gives them to the innkeeper.

cards.question: The Samaritan gives the innkeeper two denarii. What does he tell the innkeeper?

answers.text: Take care of him and I will repay you
Send him home when he can walk
Find out who did this to him

cards.text: 'Take care of him,' he said, 'and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.' An open tab for a STRANGER, when I've seen a group chat fight for three days over who owes for one box of cookies.
Then Jesus asks the expert, 'Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?'

cards.question: Jesus asks which of the three men was a neighbor to the man the robbers beat. How does the expert in the law answer?

answers.text: The one who showed him mercy
The one who came by first

cards.question: Jesus sends the expert in the law off to show ___ just like the Samaritan did.

cards.text: He asked who his neighbor was, and Jesus told him, 'Go and do likewise.' He came in to test the Teacher, friend, and he walks out with an ASSIGNMENT.

findings.problem: The opening sentence retells Luke 10:28 when it says Jesus just told the expert he was right, before the card moves to Luke 10:29. Citing only Luke 10:29 is too narrow; the card should cite Luke 10:28-29 or remove the recap.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: None of the earlier cards reveals or sets up the expert's motive for asking his follow-up question. The baker cannot reason out the unseen word "justify" rather than "humble" or "comfort," so this blank tests wording rather than an informed understanding of the moment.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the man fell into the hands of robbers. It gives no basis for reasoning that they beat him rather than bound or chased him, making the unseen word in the blank a guess.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The preceding card introduces the Samaritan and supplies background from John 4:9, but it does not establish his response when he sees the man. The earlier cards do not give the baker enough context to reason out "compassion" instead of "doubts" or "fear."

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card retells the expert's neighbor question from Luke 10:29 and his original test of Jesus from Luke 10:25, as well as quoting Luke 10:37. Its citation of only Luke 10:37 does not cover what the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
